name: National Democracy
summary: National Democracy (Endecja) is the Polish nationalist movement founded by Roman Dmowski and others in the 1880s-90s. It holds that the ethnic, Catholic Polish nation is the highest political unit, that international life is a struggle between strong and weak nations, and that minorities, especially Jews and Germans, must be Polonised or removed. It replaced class struggle with national unity, backed the Polish middle class, and in the interwar years moved toward authoritarian, religious corporatism.
scope: The Polish Endecja of Roman Dmowski and the Popular National Union, National Party and Camp of Great Poland, c. 1893-1939 (Thoughts of a Modern Pole, 1902; Church, Nation and State, 1927). It excludes unrelated 'national democracy' movements (such as the Philippine one, audited separately) and post-1945 successors. Questions on modern issues are inferred from its Catholic nationalist principles and mostly marked low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Endecja never addressed health care; its middle-class, Catholic communitarian nationalism would accept state provision for the national body but without a doctrinal commitment.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No stated wage policy; Endecja backed Polish middle-class business and also wanted workers integrated into the nation, so adherents would split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Dmowski favoured Polish private enterprise but subordinated economics to national strength, so markets were a tool rather than a principle.

public-ownership.rationale: Its base was the middle class and petty bourgeoisie, which favoured private Polish enterprise; nationalisation was a socialist idea it opposed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented tax programme; nationalist solidarity might favour burdening non-Polish capital but not the Polish middle class.

unions-good.rationale: It rejected class struggle and worked for national organisation under its own national unions, so independent class-based unions were viewed warily.

property-fundamental.rationale: Dmowski's politics defended the Polish middle class and small property owners against socialism, though property remained subordinate to the nation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed directly; Endecja wanted Polish ownership of the economy more than regulation as such.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not a stated target; nationalist solidarity within the Polish nation sits uneasily with cutting welfare, though welfare was not a priority.

worker-ownership.rationale: It stood against socialist ideas of collective ownership and favoured class cooperation under the nation, so worker ownership was not part of its programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The authoritarian, security-minded Camp of Great Poland would back state powers against perceived enemies; inferred as terrorism was not an issue then.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; a Catholic, disciplined national-moral outlook implies disapproval of recreational drug use.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Its leaders and press were themselves the target of such laws and used inflammatory anti-Jewish rhetoric, so adherents would reject restrictions as limits on national expression.

strong-leader.rationale: After 1926 the Camp of Great Poland turned toward corporatist authoritarianism admired from Italian Fascism, though Dmowski himself defended parliament earlier.

state-harmful.rationale: Dmowski demanded a strongly organised, disciplined national body, and the nation-state was the sole unit that mattered, making anarchism the opposite of the creed.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; ND stressed a disciplined armed nation but also state order.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Camp of Great Poland stressed discipline, order and national defence and fielded its own fighting squads, so a stronger security apparatus fits.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic nationalist morality implies opposition.

rehabilitation.rationale: No stated penal doctrine; adherents likely favoured order and punishment but this was not defining.

traditional-family.rationale: Dmowski's later work treats Catholic family and national morality as foundations of the nation, and the Camp advocated strongly religious corporatism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: A Catholic nationalist movement committed to traditional morality; the issue is anachronistic but the stance is clear from principles.

abortion-legal.rationale: Dmowski held Catholicism to be integral to the Polish nation, and nationalist concern with population strength points firmly against legal abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: In Church, Nation and State (1927) Dmowski argued Poland is Catholic in the full sense and that Catholicism is part of what makes the nation.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: ND saw ethnic minorities as threats to national unity and favoured Polonisation, so remedial programmes for minorities were opposed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic nationalist outlook assumes natural sex roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Endecja's core aim was the survival of Polish culture against Germanisation and Russification, pursuing independence through education and culture.

gradual-change.rationale: After 1864 it favoured organic work and culture over uprisings, but later radicalised into the Camp of Great Poland and offshoots.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anachronistic; its demand for ethnic homogeneity and Jewish emigration implies hostility to inflows of other nationalities.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Dmowski held that in relations between nations there is only strength and weakness, so supranational bodies would not override national interests.

free-trade.rationale: Dmowski's economic nationalism and boycotts favoured Polish interests; he also sought control of resources like coal and oil, implying protection.

nation-first.rationale: Dmowski called for a healthy national egoism and made the nation-state the only unit that counted, rejecting the Romantic idea of Poland as the Christ of Nations.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Dmowski saw only strength and weakness among nations; moral intervention for foreign humans would not be a priority, though not directly addressed.

open-borders.rationale: It wanted a homogeneous Polish nation-state and the emigration of Jews; open borders contradict this.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; the movement valued national strength and Polish economic advancement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic, with no doctrinal basis for either side.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Dmowski urged Poles toward modern business and science, but he didn't make technology a solution to all problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; a power-oriented doctrine would favour national energy and military capacity.

revolution-justified.rationale: It opposed armed uprising after 1864 and Dmowski rejected Piłsudski's insurrectionary plans, though the Camp later spoke of toppling the Sanacja.

experts-over-public.rationale: No clear position; ND mobilised a mass national movement but also an elite-led cadre.

central-planning.rationale: It opposed socialism and favoured the private Polish middle class, so central planning was alien to it.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; socialist-style ownership by workers or the public was rejected by a movement based on the middle class.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source documents any ND view on land taxation, and no principle of the movement points either way.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Dmowski defended the Polish propertied middle class, but nothing in the sources addresses inheritance tax, so adherents plausibly split.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; a unconditional state payout runs against its nationalist work-and-discipline ethos.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism and the push for Polish control of industry imply tariffs, though the sources don't mention tariff policy explicitly.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Dmowski wanted a strong Polish economy but favoured private initiative; adherents are mixed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: It championed the Polish middle class and petty bourgeoisie as the core of the nation and encouraged Poles to enter business and trade.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A anti-socialist movement built on private enterprise would find abolishing wages absurd.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; no sign of monetary radicalism.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Camp of Great Poland was a broad national front, not a single ruling party; National Democrats fought the Sanacja regime's authoritarianism and wanted their own party in a parliament, though later corporatist ideas leaned authoritarian.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Endecja was a modern nationalist movement oriented to the nation rather than a dynasty; it admired the Piast kingdom as an ethnic model but not monarchy as such.

democracy-best.rationale: The party worked through parliament and elections (Duma, Sejm) and favoured a strong legislature in 1921, but radicalised after 1926 toward authoritarian corporatism, so adherents are split.

direct-votes.rationale: Dmowski found even the parliamentary Sejm too chaotic; mass plebiscites were not part of the doctrine.

workers-councils.rationale: It was the sworn opponent of socialist and council-based politics, centred on the nation rather than class.

right-to-secede.rationale: Dmowski wanted a unitary Polish nation-state and the Polonisation of Belarusians, Ukrainians and Lithuanians in the Kresy, ruling out minority secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Social Darwinist ideas of strong and weak nations and the demand for a disciplined organised army imply some hierarchy, but ND is not explicit on natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Camp of Great Poland had fighting squads and its youth wings used violence against Jewish students, while Dmowski himself preferred boycotts to violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Dmowski's creed that relations between nations are decided by strength and weakness and his praise of a disciplined army point to struggle as formative.

separate-church-state.rationale: Dmowski held that Catholicism is part of what makes the Polish nation, and the Camp advocated strongly religious corporatism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholicism was integral to national identity but the movement wanted a national, not canon-law, state; not stated directly.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A movement built around a strong disciplined national state would reject privatised defence.

military-superiority.rationale: Dmowski saw international life as a struggle between strong and weak nations, so national strength including arms is valued, though his foreign policy was cautious.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Dmowski held Poland should be a nation-state and rejected the multiethnic Commonwealth, and the Piast concept favoured an ethnically and religiously homogeneous Poland.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Dmowski rejected socialism for placing class above the nation and treated nations in struggle as the force of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: It opposed socialism and egalitarian class politics, favouring the national community and Polish middle class.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement demanded national dominance in its own lands, not authority for non-state peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; its power-politics worldview offers no support for reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Dmowski opposed supra-national ideas (though he flirted with Neo-Slavism briefly and allied with Russia against Germany), centring on the Polish nation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Dmowski's explicit doctrine of healthy national egoism treats pursuit of national interest as morally right, though individual selfishness was subordinate to the nation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Dmowski's nationalist ethics puts the nation above individuals and demands that Poles be a disciplined, organised body.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental questions do not appear in the movement's documented concerns; its focus was national and cultural survival.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalist concern for the strength of the Polish nation implies favouring numbers; not stated directly.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Dmowski urged Poles to turn to business and science as modern enterprises, so he did not reject industrial civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Dmowski urged modern science and enterprise but valued continuity of tradition and Church, so adherents split.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; Catholic nationalism is likely sceptical.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the doctrine, and its organic nationalism would be suspicious.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; a security-minded authoritarian tendency would favour state access.

restore-past-order.rationale: It invoked the medieval Piast model but was a modern nationalist movement aiming at a new, organised nation-state rather than restoring the old order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Dmowski prided himself on pragmatic politics and anti-romanticism, yet was driven by firm nationalist doctrine.

direct-action.rationale: The movement worked through legal and parliamentary channels and education, though the Camp later spoke of revolutionary methods.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; Dmowski's Social Darwinist realism treats means as instruments of national strength.

return-to-foraging.rationale: It exalted national strength and modern business and science, which is incompatible with primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Alien to a movement of the middle class and national enterprise.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist distribution contradicts its anti-socialist, private-property middle-class base.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for national strength and Polish business profit, not a socialist use-economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rejects the Marxist class analysis and championed Polish business and the petty bourgeoisie.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dmowski explicitly rejected socialism and put nation above class, so class dictatorship was the opposite of its programme.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation is a socialist programme the movement fought.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Dmowski understood war as an outcome of national struggle for strength, not capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: A statist nation-first movement does not hold taxation to be theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Catholic national morality implies the state may enforce moral and national duties beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Dmowski rejected liberalism for placing the individual above the nation; the nation holds primary rights.

conscription.rationale: Dmowski called for a disciplined, organised national army and ranked duty to the nation above the individual.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Dmowski rejected liberal individualism; the nation binds its members and he wanted minorities removed rather than free to leave on their terms.

state-as-business.rationale: The nation is not a customer relationship; Dmowski put nation and duty before individuals.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; adherents unlikely to frame it in these terms.

media-academia-power.rationale: The movement's press and Camp rhetoric attacked supposed hostile elites, yet this exact claim is not documented.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Dmowski drew on Social Darwinism and radical nationalism, which often assumed hereditary national character, though race science is not directly cited.

organic-representation.rationale: The Camp of Great Poland advocated religious corporatism, implying representation through bodies and estates rather than competing parties.

total-state.rationale: Corporatist authoritarian but Catholic, and Dmowski kept the Church independent and resisted copying fascist models too closely.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement sought to rebuild an independent, organised and disciplined Polish nation, and its anti-Sanacja Camp wanted national renewal, though 'decadence' language is not documented.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Dmowski's line claimed Upper Silesia, Pomerania, Danzig and southern East Prussia, and Poland's expansion westward at German expense was core; yet he disliked eastern federal conquests.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Modern mass nationalism; it opposed feudal arrangements.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of its modern middle-class nationalism.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Dmowski's anti-romantic realism takes truth as discoverable; not addressed directly.

universal-morality.rationale: Dmowski held that between nations there is neither right nor wrong, yet the movement endorsed Catholic moral teaching; split.

single-common-good.rationale: It saw the nation as a single interest overriding class and party and rejected class politics.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Dmowski saw Zionism as part of a wider Jewish ambition and advocated Jewish emigration from Poland, though not explicitly a state in Palestine.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; Poles abroad vs minorities issues unclear.

revive-national-language.rationale: Polish language was central to cultural survival under Germanisation and Russification, though revival of a dead tongue is not directly relevant.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Alien to its class-collaborationist, hierarchical nationalism.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education mattered to ND as a tool of national culture, but nothing documents a view on funding mechanisms like vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Dmowski's economics centred on Polish ownership rather than fiscal doctrine, so no clear position follows.

economic-freedom.rationale: It supported Polish private business but was not liberal; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Dmowski sought organised national discipline backed by institutions, not rule by moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement's founding goal was Polish independence and a Polish nation-state; Dmowski secured recognition at Paris 1919, though for others he rejected minority claims.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; the strength-and-weakness view implies freedom of action, but not stated.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dmowski came to regard Catholicism as essential to the nation, though he valued hard-headed realism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: It restricted national resources to the Polish nation and favoured national over minority interests.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Its ethos of discipline and national duty is consistent, but welfare policy wasn't discussed.

class-collaboration.rationale: National Democracy replaced class struggle with national unity, with cross-class support from the intelligentsia, lower middle class and youth.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage was the means of national survival under partition; the movement opposed sacrificing it.

dominated-front.rationale: Dmowski allied with Western powers (France) and Russia pragmatically; a bloc against the West is not in his thought.

workers-nation.rationale: National Democracy organised workers on a national basis against the PPS and internationalist socialism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Catholic traditional outlook implies distinct roles, though women's role is not documented.

ban-interest.rationale: Dmowski backed Polish business and finance; some Catholic currents were suspicious of usury, but not Endecja.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Its programme was Polonisation, boycotts and emigration of Jews, not formal racial segregation as in Jim Crow, although later numerus clausus approached it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Dmowski held the nation-state to be the highest unit and rejected the Marxist class view.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Dmowski claimed Silesian coal and Galician oil for Poland, so extraction was valued; policy otherwise not documented.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: It promoted Polonisation of minorities in Poland; this applies to resident minorities more than new immigrants.

elite-replacement.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement did believe in Jewish conspiracy but not mass immigration.

proportional-representation.rationale: The 1921 Sejm used proportional lists, with Dmowski favouring a strong legislature, but he never took a stand on the method.

national-mission.rationale: Dmowski rejected Romantic messianism of Poland as the Christ of Nations in favour of national egoism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: A Catholic nationalist movement would deny that society systematically advantages men; inferred from its traditionalism since sources never discuss it.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Camp attacked Piłsudski's Sanacja and the Judeo-Masonic circles it saw around the presidency, so hostility to political elites fits.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Social Darwinist strands might attract eugenic ideas, but Catholic doctrine in the movement would resist state interference with procreation; inferred only.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; a nationalist-security stance suggests resisting.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A corporatist, Catholic and nationalist state with wide aims, not minimal.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Dmowski judged Jews too numerous to assimilate and encouraged separation, yet this does not directly cover racial marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: It treated nations as unequal in worth and minorities as threats, but did not deny the personal dignity of Poles; contested.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The question concerns Marxist-Leninist theory; as an anti-socialist movement ND has no position and no reason to take one.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not a question ND addressed; its own claims were to historic and ethnic Polish lands, not settler projects abroad.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A unitary nation-state favoured uniform law, but Catholic canon law influence unaddressed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Dmowski tied Polishness to Catholicism, which might favour discouraging leaving it, but no source documents a legal restriction.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: An Indian-context question with no bearing on Polish nationalism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Catholicism seen as essential to Polish identity, so religious instruction in schools belongs there.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A doctrine of socialist states; ND had no stake in it beyond opposing socialism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: It used parliaments and elections early on, but placed the nation above individual will.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism suggests it, though not documented.

population-transfer.rationale: Dmowski advocated emigration of Polish Jews, and the Piast concept envisioned pressure on Germans to leave.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Dmowski's creed that only strength and weakness count between nations rejects such an absolute.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Dmowski, a Social Darwinist, saw international life as a struggle of strong and weak nations and stated there is only strength and weakness.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The authoritarian bent suggests suppressing enemies such as communists, though National Democrats were themselves targeted by the Sanacja.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican-theory concept absent from ND texts; the movement framed freedom as national independence.

separated-powers.rationale: Dmowski favoured a strong legislature and weak presidency to check Piłsudski, but later authoritarian currents differed.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rejected Marxism and class politics; though the movement had its own cadre structure.

priority-to-poor.rationale: ND put the nation as a whole first and supported the middle class, so special priority for the poor is neither endorsed nor opposed in sources.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A modern British policy; ND had no housing programme documented in the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Opposition to class struggle suggests restriction, but not documented.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists wanted population strength.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Dmowski held ethnic minorities weakened the nation and rejected the Commonwealth's multiethnic tolerance as a cause of its fall.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to disciplined organisation and national elite.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The authoritarian Camp implies yes, but not directly documented.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed, and its pro-business middle-class base would be mixed on it.

party-controls-media.rationale: The movement was an opposition press to Sanacja and wanted a free voice; a ruling-party monopoly was not its aim.

party-commands-army.rationale: Dmowski opposed Piłsudski's personal control of the army; the nation, not a party, should hold it.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: It wanted restrictive membership defined by ethnicity and favoured removing minorities.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Egalitarian pay caps are a socialist device; ND's elite-led parliamentary tradition would not adopt them, though it is not documented.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Dmowski demanded a strongly organised, disciplined body in place of a loose mob.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Dmowski saw only strong and weak nations and made the nation-state supreme.

head-commands-forces.rationale: In 1921 Dmowski's camp wanted a weak presidency and strong parliament specifically to deny Piłsudski.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Dmowski wanted the Catholic church autonomous and hierarchical as part of the nation.

clerical-rule.rationale: Catholicism essential to nation, but no clerical rule; Dmowski wanted a national state with the Church independent.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A patriotic movement; it allied with Russia then the West in WWI and never wanted defeat of Poland's side.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Catholic moral-nationalist outlook implies it, though undocumented.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The 1921 constitution debate concerned a weak presidency, but term limits for re-election were not a documented ND issue.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall conflicts with Dmowski's preference for disciplined, organised representation, though it was not discussed directly.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Dmowski prioritised alliances with France and the Western powers to secure Poland.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Absurd to a property-minded middle-class movement.

people-in-arms.rationale: Dmowski wanted a disciplined organised army; spontaneous citizen armies fit Romantic uprisings he rejected.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; urban middle-class base but peasantry cherished as nation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement's own support came from the intelligentsia.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Dmowski's strong-and-weak nation Social Darwinism ranks nations.

death-penalty.rationale: Authoritarian and law-and-order leanings imply yes; not documented.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Dmowski came to treat Catholicism as inseparable from Polish identity, so a Catholic nationalist movement would reject secular sex and gender education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Catholic-nationalist adherents would favour religion in schools but evolution versus creationism was not a documented issue.

restrict-pornography.rationale: A movement committed to Catholic public morality would support such laws, as inferred from its religious corporatism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: It defined the nation as ethnic Polish and Catholic, so descent over birthplace.

minority-language-support.rationale: The movement promoted Polonisation of Germans, Belarusians, Jews, Lithuanians and Ukrainians, the opposite of minority language support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: A Catholic nationalist state favours one uniform national religious framework.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Dmowski demanded discipline and organisation, the opposite of eccentric individualism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Nation-first realism provides no basis for relief to other countries, but the topic is anachronistic for the period.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: It wanted Polish control of the economy against Jewish and German competition, but not a property transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: ND worked inside the Sejm and shaped the 1921 constitution, but no view on a special assembly is documented.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Camp's authoritarian drift might allow it, yet its documented aims were national and religious rather than developmental.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: National egoism and strength-weakness view reject international duties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; the power-politics outlook favours national capability.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Dmowski wanted a weak presidency elected by parliament in 1921.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not a documented ND issue, and the period predates the modern question.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims on Silesia, Pomerania, Danzig as national lands were core; ND criticised ceding.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property was defended for the middle class yet subordinated to the nation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: ND opposed the USSR as a hostile power and socialist state; whether it was state capitalist is a Marxist debate it did not enter.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy did not exist as a concern for the movement.

collective-defense.rationale: Dmowski prized alliance with France and West for Poland's security.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: It insisted on Polish claims against partitioning powers, so annexations without consent were illegitimate; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Dmowski argued the Church is part of the nation in Church, Nation and State, rejecting curbs on it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A symbolic head above party was not discussed; he wanted a weak presidency.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: It aimed to Polonise minorities and keep the Kresy within Poland.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Dmowski rejected federalism and the multiethnic Commonwealth in favour of a unitary Polish nation-state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Dmowski's modern nationalism rejected divine ruler ideas; Catholic and national, not dynastic.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No documented view on the structure of income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Social Darwinist outlook with national character as inherited trait.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: It fought Piłsudski's authoritarian disregard for law and favoured constitutional parliament.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic for an early twentieth-century movement.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-regime theory is not in ND texts; the movement favoured parliament and a weak presidency.

leader-cult.rationale: Camp of Great Poland partly admired fascism but Dmowski opposed copying fascist models; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law of this kind was not addressed, and Catholic traditionalism offers no clear presumption.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate about socialist states that ND never took part in.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; but ND's Polonisation did suggest breaking German-owned estates, hence low.

refugee-return.rationale: National Democrats planned that Germans would leave, with no return, and pressed Jews to emigrate.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Early Piast-based claims covered areas with a substantial Polish-speaking population, a co-ethnic basis.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: ND treated Catholicism as part of national identity but did not call for penal punishment of leaving it.

women-must-cover.rationale: A Polish Catholic movement would find compulsory covering alien to its customs; inferred, as sources are silent.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Dmowski flirted with Neo-Slavism tactically but placed the Polish nation first.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The movement sought Polonisation of minorities, not self-governing minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Dmowski urged Jewish emigration rather than integration with equal rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rejected Marxist materialism; nations and national will drive history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Dmowski wanted Polish control of the economy, not an antitrust programme; no documented view.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not documented; adherents might be nationalist about saving Polish firms or fiscally conservative.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: National majority primacy appealed, but ND fought for legality against Sanacja.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender parity quotas run against the traditional Catholic social order the movement defended.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: ND favoured Polish ownership and protection of national interests but did not call for closing off trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Modern trade-treaty policy, anachronistic for the movement, so no clear position.

moral-incentives.rationale: Duty to the nation is central yet material gains for the Polish middle class also were.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: It had fighting squads but no revolutionary doctrine of foco.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: ND was a middle-class modern movement not tied to titles, but it did not campaign against the nobility either.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement pursued independence through education and culture centred on the Polish nation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Polonisation of eastern minorities as bringing civilisation; Dmowski's talk of multiplying civilisational efforts.

patriotic-education.rationale: National Democracy aimed to preserve Polish identity through education and culture.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: It saw preferences for minorities as unacceptable and championed ethnic Poles.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform ideas do not appear in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not directly discussed; a pro-business middle-class movement.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Piast concept deliberately turned away from the Jagiellonian eastern realm toward ethnic Polish western lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dmowski wanted Poland to compete economically; withdrawal from the world economy fits neither his realism nor his business orientation.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist concept that ND, as an anti-Marxist movement, would reject; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: It favoured boycotts of Jewish shops and preferential Polish economic life, though state-enforced numerus clausus implies state not liberty.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not addressed; it fought for national legal order but no documented view on entrenchment.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; yet Dmowski opposed the Minority Rights Treaty imposed at Versailles, so imposed treaties draw suspicion.

elective-rulers.rationale: Modern nationalists, not dynastic; Dmowski worked via elections and parliament.

minority-veto.rationale: Dmowski demanded disciplined organisation under majority decision.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Opposition to Piłsudski's coup and Sanacja implies resisting unconstitutional rule; not directly stated.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Dmowski favoured a strong legislature and weak presidency in the 1921 constitution.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not documented among the movement's aims.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A conventional view that adherents would likely hold, though the sources never discuss it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Catholic social ethos and national solidarity suggest it; not documented.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Dmowski demanded active national organisation and action rather than withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt-school style claim never engaged by ND, so no position is inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis outside the movement's intellectual world.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is Marxist in origin, which ND rejected, but it also never discussed the thesis.

native-born-offices.rationale: It excluded Jews and other minorities from public life and favoured ethnic Poles in office.

party-own-road.rationale: A dispute inside the communist movement with no bearing on ND.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: National self-help (organic work) was its response to partition.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The movement's Western claims to lands lost in the partitions and held by Germany were central, and Dmowski's Line demanded them back at Paris.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not applicable; ND demanded national dominance of the Polish ethnic majority in its own state, not descendants-of-natives rules in settler states.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Camp borrowed from Italian Fascism and Dmowski praised Mussolini in 1926.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anti-communist; but also admired Italian fascism, so split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historiographical dispute outside the movement's concerns.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: A nationalist movement that valued heritage would tend to preserve monuments, though it is an anachronistic question.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Modern gender-policy debate; ND texts give no basis for a position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by ND; tradition-minded adherents could go either way.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Dmowski criticised liberal and Romantic imports and wanted institutions fitting the Polish national character.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Dmowski fought Piłsudski's military politics yet favoured discipline.

paid-care-work.rationale: Catholic family-centred outlook would treat care as a family duty, not paid labour, but this is inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Catholic traditional family ethics, which ND embraced, stress lifelong respect for parents; inferred from its traditionalism.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Chinese-style examination system is outside ND thought.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism aimed to place the economy in Polish hands.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic teaching on marriage, which Dmowski held integral to the nation, opposes easy divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandate and instant recall fit council democracy, not Dmowski's disciplined, hierarchical organisation.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension system design was not an ND concern.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Rejects collective land ideas; private smallholding.

single-official-language.rationale: The movement pushed Polonisation of Germans, Belarusians, Jews, Lithuanians and Ukrainians through the state.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: National Democrats planned land reforms to push German landowners out.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Opposed to preferences framing for minorities.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Catholic moralism might criticise consumerism but ND celebrated Polish business, so it likely splits.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not documented; the movement was cautious in foreign policy and opposed Piłsudski's adventures.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: A Cold War doctrine about socialist bloc discipline, unrelated to ND.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed; but ND described Jewish financial influence conspiratorially.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: It saw Jewish and German influence as foreign threats to the nation.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Nation-strength thinking favours a larger Polish population, though the sources never discuss family subsidies.

residents-only-property.rationale: Pressure on German landowners fits it, but local-limits specifically not documented.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee leans socialist, which ND opposed; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: International relations are struggles of strength, not shaped by regime type.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Dmowski's demand for disciplined national organisation and duty to the nation rejects any claim that law carries no obligation.

non-intervention.rationale: Strength-and-weakness realism neither endorses nor bars intervention; ND foreign policy was cautious and status-quo after 1919.

industrial-unions.rationale: ND favoured national rather than class organisation and gave no view on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Dmowski believed in an international Jewish conspiracy against Poland and that Polish Jews collaborated with Germans.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Catholic nationalist movement upheld marriage as a legal and sacramental institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The movement left no stance on freedom-of-information rights, which postdate it.

local-production.rationale: Dmowski urged Polish business but nothing documents a localist production doctrine.

informal-organisation.rationale: Dmowski explicitly wanted a strongly organised, disciplined army instead of a loose mob.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Dmowski opposed the Minority Rights Treaty imposed on Poland.

religious-nation.rationale: Dmowski's 1927 work holds that Poland is Catholic in the full sense, as the nation's people are Catholic.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: National pride; though allied with France, not submission.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A unitary national state would pool revenue nationally; inferred from its opposition to regional separatism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A Marxist distinction irrelevant to ND, which defended private property generally.

defeat-communism.rationale: Opposed socialism and Bolshevism; National Armed Forces fought the Soviets.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models were outside the movement's interests.

religion-illusion.rationale: Dmowski concluded Catholicism is essential to Polish identity.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Dmowski urged Poles into business and science and defended the middle class, which suggests acceptance of capitalist development; not stated directly.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A socialist-feminist claim that ND, defending the existing order and traditional roles, would reject; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Collective housework and childcare conflicts with the Catholic family-centred order the movement championed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: ND defended Polish language against Germanisation, but no source documents a campaign against loanwords.

treaties-binding.rationale: A question about indigenous treaties, with no ND analogue.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Communitarian anarchist-style experiments contradict ND's unitary nation-state.

majority-settlement.rationale: Polish settlement in borderlands was part of Polonisation and Piast concept.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Camp of Great Poland favoured religious corporatism, a third-way idea, though the sources do not frame it so.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Piast concept grounded claims in medieval Polish lands.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Dmowski died in 1939, before the Holocaust, and the movement's later heirs split; not addressed in sources.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Catholic moral conservatism implies support, but sources never mention the issue.

suppress-opposition.rationale: National Democrats were themselves a persecuted opposition under Sanacja.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Catholicism as part of national identity suggests state protection of religion, though no law is documented.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Poland had no overseas empire and ND never addressed colonial administration.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic-law question with no relevance to Polish nationalism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: An Islamist doctrine with no analogue in ND.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: ND stressed national unity above class and ethnicity and rejects such frameworks; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Traditional Catholic outlook; the issue is modern, inferred from principles.

assisted-dying.rationale: Catholic doctrine, which Dmowski held integral to Polish identity, opposes euthanasia.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: It saw itself as nationalist right opposing socialism.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist theory that ND rejected along with class politics.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Dmowski made Catholicism part of the nation, but he grounded political authority in the nation rather than in God directly.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: A Catholic-majority nationalist movement would not want religious dress barred, though minority dress might be different.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern employment-law dispute, not addressed.

social-market-economy.rationale: ND favoured private enterprise and national solidarity, but no documented position on a social market model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Dmowski demanded a disciplined army and valued strength.

rich-first.rationale: A development-strategy slogan from China; ND had no equivalent.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Dmowski allied with France and Russia, then West.

dynastic-succession.rationale: A modern mass-nationalist movement that took parliament as the vehicle of the nation would not back hereditary leaders.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking is not part of ND, which defended conventional private business.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Nation-first realism favours refusing outside conditions on national policy, though IMF-style lending postdates the movement; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: ND used elections and a wide base of intelligentsia and lower middle class; franchise limits were not its aim.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is alien to a traditional Catholic nationalist doctrine.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The movement worked for constitutional parliament before 1926 and opposed Piłsudski's coup, which supports rule through standing law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Dmowski excluded Jews from the national community, the closest ethnic franchise stance, though law-based exclusion is a stretch.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; Dmowski stressed disciplined organisation led by the national movement over open mass deliberation, so he would be wary of it.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; no ND text addresses transparency of government records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Catholic nationalism that treats Catholicism as national identity would favour discouraging mixed marriage with Jews; inferred, not documented.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Dmowski organised boycotts of Jewish businesses after the 1912 Duma election, and ND backed boycotts in the 1930s.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Randomly chosen deliberation conflicts with Dmowski's organised, disciplined national leadership.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Dmowski's late work treats Catholicism as the nation's settled foundation rather than something to be revised.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: ND opposed socialist redistribution yet attacked Jewish economic power, so it neither endorses nor rejects the claim cleanly.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Dmowski held Catholicism essential to nation.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Camp of Great Poland stressed discipline, order and fighting squads, which excludes abolishing the apparatus of order.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: It favoured majority national rule with Polonisation.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Catholic charity ethos fits but ND did not oppose public welfare; adherents split.

term-limits.rationale: ND never debated limits on office-holding beyond the 1921 constitution fight over a weak presidency, so no position is supported.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy conflicts with disciplined representation; anachronistic.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A twenty-first century concern with no counterpart in a movement focused on national survival and independence.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Catholic teaching and ND's embrace of it exclude women from priesthood.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Traditional Catholic family doctrine has husband as head, but the sources are silent.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Membership of the national community was ethnic and Catholic; non-citizens voting contradicts that.

rent-control.rationale: No housing programme is documented; the middle-class base might split between tenants and landlords.

abolish-ip.rationale: The movement defended private property and Polish enterprise, so abolishing patents is unlikely; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Large youth wing and the Camp's disciplined organisation, fighting squads.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement predates nuclear weapons and gives no basis for a position.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Dmowski relied on alliance with France, but basing is a modern question.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Dmowski died before such recognition practices; heirs split, and the sources do not address it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: ND defended property owners and the middle class while also valuing work, so no clean position.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Dmowski's view of life as struggle and demand for national discipline rules out pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Piast concept sees continuity back to early Polish state, though scholars treat it as myth.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Traditional Catholic outlook assumes natural sex distinctions.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Postmodern feminism is alien to ND's traditional order.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nationalist heroes; National Armed Forces fought and leaders killed.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Catholic, yet Dmowski prized pragmatic realism over spiritual crusade.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Dmowski wanted Poles united in the national state.

culture-before-state.rationale: After 1864 the movement held that independence would come through education and culture.

god-not-male.rationale: Catholic nationalism holds to traditional doctrine.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology contradicts traditional Catholic authority embraced by ND.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Dmowski backed Polish middle class, boycotts of Jewish business, and focus on economic competition between Polish Catholics and Jews.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Piast concept sought to unite Polish-speaking lands into one state; inferred for this administrative-merger framing.

independent-unions.rationale: Corporatist ND wanted organisation under national bodies rather than independent class unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Anti-socialist; it denies socialism's goals altogether.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Municipal ownership of utilities is not part of the documented ND programme.

second-chamber.rationale: Dmowski wanted a strong Sejm, but no source discusses a Senate.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership of production is a socialist or anarchist model ND rejected.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Confederal libertarian municipalism contradicts ND's centralised nation-state.

family-wage.rationale: Catholic corporatist social thought supports a living family wage, though the Endecja sources do not state it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Medical regulation did not figure in the movement, so nothing supports a lean either way.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic science-policy question with no basis in ND thought.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The Camp's security-minded authoritarianism would favour traceability; anachronistic.

person-over-state.rationale: Dmowski placed the nation above the individual and demanded duty to it; personalist limits on the state are alien to this.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Dmowski argued Catholicism is part of the nation, so a spiritual dimension of politics fits.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: ND wanted a unitary state in which central legislature holds ultimate power.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; Catholic traditionalist caution and nationalist farm interests pull in different directions.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning for environmental ends was not an ND issue.

racial-group-interests.rationale: ND saw ethnic groups, Poles above all, as having distinct interests to be defended, though 'race' was framed as nation.

racial-pride.rationale: National pride and healthy national egoism are central to Dmowski; 'race' is treated as ethnic nation.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Dmowski's strength-and-weakness doctrine and territorial claims make renouncing offensive force unlikely, though his own policy was cautious.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Polish identity defined by language and culture, though Catholicism also needed, which cuts against it.

communal-electorates.rationale: ND pursued Polonisation, not separate electorates for minorities.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Dmowski saw Germans and Jews conspiring to partition Poland.

free-public-college.rationale: ND valued education as a vehicle of national culture but documents no view on tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is a modern policy outside the movement's concerns.

future-generations.rationale: A nation outlasting its members implies duty to posterity, but the environmental angle is inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not documented; traditionalists might agree on complementary roles but the sources do not say.

arms-reduction.rationale: Dmowski's creed of strength makes broad disarmament unattractive.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Dmowski worked through diplomatic networks at Paris and treaties, but secret diplomacy is not documented.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic nationalism might favour control but nothing documents it.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A state-centred order would favour a state monopoly, although the Camp itself fielded armed squads.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Dmowski's insistence on a disciplined national army conflicts with refusal of orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: ND wanted class cooperation, which might mean bargaining or arbitration; no direct documentation.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: A modern welfare device; ND documented no social-insurance programme.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are a late-twentieth-century idea; ND gave no stance on borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Strength-and-weakness realism offers no basis for reordering in favour of other states.

smash-state-machine.rationale: It wanted to capture the state through parliament.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: ND wanted a national economic order, not freedom for communities to choose systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural-capital accounting is a modern environmental-economics idea with no ND link.

sacred-nation.rationale: Dmowski absolutised the nation as the highest unit.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; student loans were not an issue for the movement.

internal-colonialism.rationale: ND sought Polish unity; the theory was not discussed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Catholic natural-law view is plausible but Dmowski's national Darwinism argues otherwise; split.

public-service-media.rationale: ND ran its own party press and distrusted what it called hostile press, but a publicly funded independent broadcaster is a later concept.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Dmowski's Catholic exclusivity fits poorly with perennialism.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not documented; peasants were part of the nation but ND's base was urban.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; strength-oriented outlook favours retaining deterrents.

workers-own-party.rationale: It wanted workers in the national movement, opposing PPS.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; a Catholic Polish movement would readily oppose such a practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; no documented stance on women's property law.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A Balkan or South Asian linguistic dispute with no ND analogue.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: A libertarian legal theory of pollution that ND never touched.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: A tribal arrangement alien to a centralised European nation-state.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The movement had no environmental programme, so there is no basis to rank the two.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The order-focused Camp suggests favouring fixed punishments, though sentencing was not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: ND promoted Polonisation and a single national culture, which implies expecting language learning.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: ND opposed class unions and favoured national organisation, but did not take a documented stand.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification is a modern electoral-integrity dispute absent from ND sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Dmowski held Poland is Catholic in the full sense, so the state would privilege Catholicism.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Dmowski used elections but cared about national substance, and the Camp turned authoritarian; split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Catholic sexual morality, which the movement embraced, condemns it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The order-minded authoritarian Camp would probably accept it; anachronistic and inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: A Friedmanite welfare reform with no precedent in ND economics.

decide-locally.rationale: Dmowski wanted a unitary, strongly organised Polish nation-state and opposed federal schemes like Piłsudski's, though local self-government was used as a tool against Germanisation.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Camp of Great Poland's religious corporatism implies employer and worker bodies bargaining under national arbitration; the exact mechanism is not described in the pages opened.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Polish independence meant reuniting lands divided among the Prussian, Austrian and Russian partitions, a goal the movement pursued from 1886 onward.

missingStatements.text: Universities should limit the number of students admitted from a particular ethnic or religious minority.
missingStatements.rationale: National Democrats campaigned for numerus clausus and numerus nullus against Jewish students and academics in interwar Poland.
missingStatements.declined: A historical measure specific to interwar Polish nationalism; the underlying position is partly covered by minority-conspiracy and economy-in-majority-hands.

missingStatements.text: A country's foreign policy should rest on national interest and strength rather than on moral principles.
missingStatements.rationale: Dmowski wrote that between nations there is neither right nor wrong, only strength and weakness, and advocated healthy national egoism.

notes: Dmowski early on opposed violence and favoured legal, parliamentary work and boycotts; younger radicals (National Radical Camp, 1934) and the Camp of Great Poland pushed a fascist-influenced line he partly resisted. The primary source is read through quotations (Wikiquote) because full texts of Thoughts of a Modern Pole and Church, Nation and State were not freely accessible; the movement's positions on economic and modern issues are thinly documented, so many answers are inferences.
